Commentary.Commentary: Let us have a look at the records then. 67 - this is the lowest total in Bulawayo, Zimbabwe's lowest against Pakistan, the second lowest by any team against Pakistan and Zimbabwe's joint 5th lowest in ODIs overall. Ouch. Pakistan are in line to register their 5th 10-wicket win, second against Zimbabwe in ODIs. Will it happen? The second innings is about to resume...

Terrific bowling from Pakistan but to be honest, there was nothing in the pitch. Neither was there prolific swing, nor any prolonged seam movement or that much turn on offer. Zimbabwe, well, looked like they had come to work on a weekend, were scheduled a compensatory off today but were forced to come and well, were upset. Faheem was superb, with his 5-fer, hitting the deck and keeping the lines straight, while the others were decent as well.

Well, it was a you-blink-and-you-miss kind of an innings. What to type? Only three batsmen managed to reach double figures. They had no answer to the pace of Faheem, Junaid or Usman, or the spin of Yasir. A sorry, sorry performance from Zimbabwe who simply seem to be going down with every game.

OUT! Corker of a yorker and the off stump is off the ground. Faheem has his 5th. Gets down and kisses the turf. Ngarava can barely get his bat down in time and well, Zimbabwe have just managed to scrape past the half-way mark. ALL OUT FOR 67!
Now they run! Full and outside off, driven towards mid off and well, the batsmen run. Don't know why.
On middle and leg, flicked towards deep mid-wicket. A single is called for but they do not run!
Richard Ngarava is the last man in.

OUT! Given. That looked to be missing leg but Muzarabani has been given the marching orders. The googly, pitched around middle, Blessing looked to defend but missed. Seemed to be hit around the leg stump, with the ball sliding down, but well... no reviews in this country.

FOUR! Two targets achieved. First, Muzarabani gets off the mark. Second, Zimbabwe get past the lowest total posted by any opponent in ODIs against Pakistan, surpassing New Zealand's 64 in 1986 in Sharjah. Down the leg side, Muzarabani looks to flick but the ball goes off the inner half of the bat and past the keeper to the fine leg fence! The next target - 74 by New Zealand, in Sharjah, 1990.
A low full toss around off, pushed towards long on for a single.
The googly to start, around middle and off, pushed towards point.
Here comes the fifth bowler. Shadab Khan to bowl.
Very full outside off, driven straight to mid off. Only a leg bye from the over, so technically a maiden for Ashraf, whose figures read 8-2-22-4.
Solid, tight defense. Full and straight, pushed towards mid on.
A lovely line, on a length outside off, Blessing plays inside the line but misses.
A bouncer outside off, Muzarabani sways away.
Pitched outside leg, Masakadza misses his flick and the ball goes off his pads to the leg side. A leg bye taken.
Full and straight, driven straight back to the bowler.
Around off, defended watchfully. Second maiden for Yasir, whose figures read 7-2-10-1.
Tossed up very slowly around off, Blessing defends.
A short extra cover coming in... on the drive.
The googly around off, pushed back to the bowler.
On middle and leg, flicked wide of mid on.
Very well bowled. Pitched outside leg, spinning away, Muzarabani defends.
Floated outside off, driven back to the bowler.
Landed outside off, on a length, Masakadza sways away.
Full and outside off, driven through the covers a couple. Approaching that 64 now...
Full and outside off, driven straight to mid off.
A bouncer on middle, Masakadza ducks under it.
Around off, watchfully pushed towards mid off.
Usman Khan is warming up...
On a length around off, angling away, pushed towards cover.
Full and just outside off, Blessing just hangs his bat outside off and blocks.
The batsman was beaten and missed the line of the delivery.
Works it straight to short mid-wicket.
Miles outside off, left alone.
Played to the mid-wicket region by the batsman.
Full and on middle, pushed towards long on for a single.

End of the innings for Zimbabwe. Oh sorry... I thought it was a T20I. Been woken up from my slumber. The so-called ODI resumes. Zimbabwe have completed one target - getting their 50. Then achieved their second, playing out 20 overs. Now moving towards their third - the lowest ODI total by any team against Pakistan is 64 by New Zealand in Sharjah (1986).
Full and outside off, driven back to the bowler again.
Full and straight, driven nicely back to the bowler.
On middle and leg, helped through square leg for a single. He wants the second but Muzarabani is not interested.
Similar ball outside off, Wellington flays at it but misses.
A touch short outside off, Masakadza leaps and punches it towards cover.
Hits the deck hard, bowls it on a length outside off, pushed towards point.
The batsman defends it from within the crease.
Flicks this through mid-wicket for a single.
Floated generously outside off, Wellington stays back and blocks.
Much fuller, closer to the off stump, Masakadza flicks it towards mid-wicket.
Spinning in from well outside off, WM stays back and pushes it towards cover.
Full and around off, Wellington stretches to defend.
WIDE. Down the leg side, Masakadza looks to flick but misses.
A bit of a check on Muzarabani. He shows a thumbs up, indicating he is fine. Just a look at his helmet and everyone is ready.

ON THE HELMET! He is not a short guy by any means but Faheem still pings him on the grille. A short ball, a very good bouncer around off, Blessing takes his eyes off the ball and is hit on the helmet. All the Pakistan players surround him, asking whether he is fine but the tall lad is hardly perturbed.
Around off, well blocked out.
A length ball around off, watchfully defended.
Who is next? Blessing Muzarabani walks in to bat.

OUT! Four for Ashraf, 8 for Pakistan.  A length ball, straight, coming in with the angle, Murray looks to defend but the ball stays low a touch, hits the bottom half of the bat and cannons into the off stump, uprooting it. They check for the no ball but replays show that Ashraf is fine. Best figures for Faheem in ODIs.
A short ball around off, fended back to the bowler.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.

FOUR! AWESOME! A rare, rare adjective used today. But this one deserves it. Tossed up wide outside off, Masakadza reaches out and drives it wide of mid off for a boundary! The stand moves to 11 from 15 balls.
Looped up around off, Masakadza pushes it back to the bowler.
Dropped short, heaved straight to square leg.
Full on middle, pushed towards the bowler.
The googly around off, well blocked out.
Tossed up outside off, watchfully defended.
The ball strikes the batsman very low on the pads. The batsmen have run through for a single. The umpire signals a leg bye. 50 UP FOR ZIMBABWE! An achievement.
WIDE. A bouncer, wided for height.
Played to the point region by the batsman.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
On a length outside off, dabbed to third man for a single.
FOUR! That helps to give some work to the scorers. The scoreboard moves a bit. On middle and leg, flicked towards square leg. Not a soul there and the ball meets the fence.
Full and around off, watchfully defended.
On middle and leg, worked to the leg side. First wicket for Yasir - his figures read 3-1-3-1.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Full and around off, watchfully blocked out.
Wellington Masakadza comes in now.

OUT! Bowled around his legs! Oh dear... it is becoming a morning to forget for Zimbabwe, let alone a day not worth remembering. They are falling like ninepins. It is a googly outside leg, Chisoro looks to sweep but misses. The leg stump is out of the ground.
The batsman rocks onto the back foot and punches the ball. The batsmen have run through for a single.
Full and outside off, watchfully defended.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat. A wicket in each over for Ashraf in his 18 balls so far...
Into the bowlers now. Tendai Chisoro is the first of them.

OUT! Sorry, sorry state for Zimbabwe now. The lack of feet movement eventually costs Chigumbura. He was literally not interested in moving his feet at all. Ashraf bowls this slightly wider than the previous one, Elton pushes at it without moving his feet and nicks it behind. 6 down are Zimbabwe.
Tighter from the bowler. Elton defends.

FOUR! HAMMERED! He has hit that through the line. Full and wide outside off, Chigumbura reaches out, does not bother moving his feet and blasts it through the covers. Sarfraz is not happy with the width given by the bowler.
Full and straight, Murray plays all around it, looking to flick but misses and is hit on the pads. An LBW appeal ensues but that was going down leg. A leg bye taken.
On a length outside off, punched straight to point.
Landed around off, pushed towards cover. Second maiden of the innings.
Full and outside off, pushed towards cover.
The quicker one, outside off, the googly, pushed towards the bowler.
Superb bowling. The leg spin now, Elton just about picks it at the last moment and thrusts his bat in front of his pad.
Looks to drive now but gets an inside edge off the googly towards the leg side.
Tossed up outside off, Chigumbura looks to punch but gets a bottom edge to the off side.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Back of a length on off, Chigumbura pushes it through third man for a run.
FOUR! Off the mark in style! Full and outside off, Chigumbura strokes it through cover-point. No man in the deep and a boundary results.
Elton Chigumbura strides out to the middle.

OUT! Half the side back in the hut and Pakistan have not even bowled 15 overs. Ashraf gets his second in 4 balls. He spears in a full ball which comes back in late, Chibhabha plants his front foot way too across and misses the flick. It hits his pads, the players appeal and even before the bowler could complete his appeal, the umpire raises his finger. That is how plumb it was.
Fuller in length on off, Murray strokes it through covers and takes a run.
Back of a length on middle, Murray works it to mid-wicket.
Punches it down to long off and gets to the other end. 2 from the leg spinner's first over.
Defended off the back foot by the batsman.
This time finds the gap on the leg side. Slightly shorter on middle, Chibhabha nudges it through mid-wicket and gets to the other end.
Works it with the angle but finds the man at square leg.
Floats it up on middle, Chibhabha defends it onto the ground.
The slider first up on middle, Chibhabha works it to mid-wicket.
Powerplay 2 has been signaled! Now 4 fielders can be placed outside the ring till the 40th over, if the innings last till then. Also spin for the first time today as Yasir Shah is into the attack.
Back of a length on off, it is pushed to covers. End of Powerplay 1 and it is a brilliant one for Pakistan. Zimbabwe are 30 for 4 after it.
Ryan Murray walks in at no. 6.

OUT! Another one bites the dust! Ashraf strikes in his first over. He comes running in and lands it on a length just outside off. Moor maybe could have left that but he goes fishing after it. The ball takes the outside edge and flies towards Azam at widish first slip. He stretches his hands out towards his right and takes a very good catch.

Good fielding! Full and on off, the batsman drives it towards covers. Zaman there runs to his right, dives and makes a good stop. He can't stop the single but saves at least two more for his side. Made up for the misfield earlier.
The batsman works it down the leg side.
Back of a length on off, the batsman guides it down to third man for a run.
Good length on middle, Chibhabha defends it towards mid-wicket for a quick run.
Faheem Ashraf is the new bowler.
Fuller in length on off, the batsman strokes it to mid off. A run a wicket from the over, Junaid Khan's figures read 5-1-7-2.
On a length again outside off, the batsman need not play at those.
On a length around off, the batsman makes a leave.
WIDE! Goes for another bumper but this time it is a little too high. Wide signaled.
Peter Moor walks in next. He got a half century in the last game and Zimbabwe would love it if he could get another here.

OUT! Wicket no. 99 for Junaid Khan! The short ball does the trick for him. It is a well-directed one and Musakanda goes for the hook. He only manages to get a glove to it and Sarfraz behind the stumps completes his second catch. JK is all pumped up and Zimbabwe slip further.
Fuller in length on off, the batsman drives it back to the bowler.
Tight line and length by Khan! On off and on a length. The batsman defends it solidly.
Back of a length on off, the batsman blocks it. This is what the Zimbabwe batsmen are not able to do. After getting a boundary of the last ball, they should be looking to rotate strike.
FOUR! A much-needed one! Short and on the body. Chibhabha picks it early and pulls it over backward square leg for a boundary.
Back of a length on off, Chibhabha defends it onto the ground.
Shorter in length, Chibhabha pulls it through mid-wicket. There is a man in the deep who runs to his right and keeps it down to two.
Good length again on off, guided to point.
Length ball, this one skids off the surface. Chibhabha tries to block it but the ball takes the outside edge and goes towards cover-point.
Wide outside off, the umpire signals it a wide.
A dot end another successful over for Pakistan. 2 runs and a wicket. On a length around off, kept out.
Tarisai Musakanda walks out to the middle.

OUT! In the air... this time it carries! The big fish, if there is any in this Zimbabwe team is walking back. A well-deserved wicket for Junaid Khan. He lands this just ahead of a length on off. Hamilton tries to clear mid off but gets it nowhere off the middle. It lobs towards Yasir Shah there who runs in and takes a good tumbling catch. Zimbabwe lose their second within Powerplay 1 and are in trouble.
Length again on off, Masakadza tries to defend but gets an inside edge onto his pads.
Fuller in length on middle, it is stroked to mid on.

In the air... and again it goes on the bounce to the man at third man. Chibhabha uses his feet and tries to go over mid off. A shot in anger you can say. He though gets a thick outside edge and the ball flies towards third man. He comes running in but the ball does not carry. He collects it on the bounce and the batsmen take one.
Good length on off, Masakadza tries to defend but the ball goes off the inner half towards square leg for a single.
Just ahead of a length on off, Chibhabha defends it towards mid off. Good over for the hosts, six from it.
On a length around off, guided down to third man for a run.

In the air... and on the bounce to third man! Short and outside off, Chibhabha goes for the cut but the ball takes the top edge, bounces in front of third man who collects it and throws it to the keeper as the batsmen complete one.
OOOO! The bowler did not like being hit for a boundary there. He bends his back on this delivery and bowls a bumper. Chibhabha goes for the pull but is beaten by pace.
FOUR! Nicely played! On a length around off, Chibhabha plants his front foot forward and strokes it through covers for a boundary. His first.
A little too wide outside off, the batsman is in no mood to go after it.
Good delivery! On a length around off, this one moves away. HM tries to drive it but the ball goes off the outer half through point for a couple.
A bouncer on middle, evaded.
On the off stump, kept out.
Attacks the off stump, the batsman defends it onto the ground.
Good length outside off, left alone.
Chibhabha gets off the mark, courtesy a misfield. On a length around off, it is pushed towards Zaman at covers. He misfields and concedes a run. Sarfraz is not happy with the effort.
NOPE! Khan errs in line and bowls it on the pads, Masakadza works it through square leg and runs two.
Fuller in length on off, the batsman strokes it towards covers who makes a good stop. 11 dots in a row, can this be the second consecutive maiden?
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Shorter in length on middle, Masakadza defends it back to the bowler.
Make that 8! Length ball outside off, the batsman shoulders arms to it.
Fuller on middle, Hamilton works it to mid-wicket. 7 dots in a row after the boundary.
Dot to end! A maiden for Junaid. He has been really good with his line and length till now. On off, Chibhabha keeps it out.
Good change in length by Khan! Bowls a bouncer and a well-directed one. Chibhabha does well to duck under it.
Hits the length hard on middle, the batsman defends it back to the bowler.
Almost! The sucker ball outside off, Chibhabha goes after it but misses.
Pulls his length back a little on off, CC tries to drive but gets it off the inner half towards mid on.
Fuller in length on off, no swing on offer for Khan. Chibhabha eases it to mid off.
FOUR! A good end to the over for Zimbabwe! First boundary for them today. Full and on off, Masakadza strokes it past the bowler and it races to the fence.
Very wide outside off, the batsman makes a leave. Not signaled wide by the umpire as he might have felt it was inside the tramline.
Good delivery! Good use of the angle I should say! On a length around off, this one angles away from the batsman after pitching. Hamilton tries to defend but is beaten.
Hits the length around off, Masakadza defends it onto the ground.
Hamilton Masakadza is the new man in.

OUT! EDGED AND TAKEN! Usman Khan draws first blood. Not a great delivery but a poor shot by Masvaure. He was watchful till now but he ran out of patience. This is slightly short and outside off. Masvaure tries to force it through the off side, without moving his feet. That proves to be his undoing as the ball takes the outside edge and settles into the mitts of Sarfraz Ahmed. He takes it, appeals and the umpire raises his finger. Early breakthrough for Pakistan and a poor debut for Masvaure.
Wide outside off, a loosener to begin. The batsman need not play at those.
Usman Khan will bowl from the other end with the second new ball. A slip in place for him.
A good delivery to end a tight first over by Junaid Khan. On a length around off, it slants across the batsman. Chibhabha leaves it alone.

Zimbabwe are underway, not in a convincing manner though. On a length outside off, this one shapes away a touch. Masvaure tries to block it off the back foot but the ball takes the outside edge, goes past the second slip fielder and down to third man for a run.
On a length outside off, Masvaure covers his off stump and shoulders arms to it.
Bowls it on the stumps this time. PM walks across and works it to the man at mid-wicket.
Another length ball outside off, no swing on offer this time. Masvaure makes another leave.
A little shape for Khan and a good start by the bowler! He lands it on a length around off, this one shapes away. Masvaure first thinks of playing at it but then pulls out of the shot.

We are all set for the action to begin. The umpires make their way out to the middle along with the Pakistan players. Chamu Chibhabha and Prince Masvaure are the openers for Zimbabwe. The latter will be on strike and he will face Junaid Khan. Here we go...

TEAM CHANGES - Plenty for the home side. 4 to be precise. Prince Masvaure (when did he get added to the squad?), Elton Chigumbura, Tendai Chisoro and Richard Ngarava get a chance to play today. Let me check who all miss out. Brian Chari is the first, then Donald Tiripano, Liam Roche and finally Tendai Chatara! Yes, first rank in byhearting!!! Pakistan have easier changes to remember - Yasir Shah gets a chance today. The last time he played an ODI was against England in Nottingham on August 30, 2016. Junaid Khan makes a comeback too, after featuring last against Sri Lanka in an ODI in Sharjah on 20th October, 2017.
TOSS TIME - Zimbabwe win another toss. Again, they elect to bat first. Can they put up a decent total today?
WEATHER - It is another cold morning in Bulawayo and conditions certainly will not be helpful to the fielding side.

Another day, another game. How it came? That is all Zimbabwe have been thinking from the time they have started playing the tri-series. Did not win a single match against Australia or Pakistan and have not won any here. They have lost the first set if you consider it as a tennis game - 6-0, you see. Hello and a warm welcome - oops, COLD welcome to the third ODI between Zimbabwe and Pakistan in Bulawayo. A must-win game for Zimbabwe not only as far as the series is concerned - but for their own growth and future.
